The images, icons, and text that you see in a Flutter app are all widgets." architectural-overview.md: "Widgets form a hierarchy based on composition. The lesson's arrow gloss ("points from a widget to one it contains") holds as ancestor-to-descendant; framework widgets in between are not denied.

claim_verdicts.source: Flutter 3.47.2 SDK source: packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/app.dart:840-847 (WidgetsApp.title, reused by MaterialApp.title)
claim_verdicts.evidence: "A one-line description used by the device to identify the app for the user. ... On the web it is used as the page title, which shows up in the browser's list of open tabs." The AppBar text comes from `AppBar(title: const Text('Đơn Hàng'))` (product_list_screen.dart L33). Round-1 minor resolved.

FutureBuilder: "Creates a widget that builds itself based on the latest snapshot of interaction with a [Future]." _FutureBuilderState._subscribe: `widget.future!.then((T data) { ... setState(() { _snapshot = AsyncSnapshot<T>.withData(ConnectionState.done, data); }); })`. AsyncSnapshot.data: "The latest data received by the asynchronous computation." Note: the setState is in FutureBuilder's own state, so only FutureBuilder rebuilds (see issue in 'Beginners often think').

issues.quote: You notice this when the products arrive and the list replaces the spinner, while the title bar, which is described the same way both times, is left as it was.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and not true of this code. When the future completes, `setState` runs inside `_FutureBuilderState` (Flutter 3.47.2 widgets/async.dart:643), so only the FutureBuilder's `builder` runs again. `_ProductListScreenState.build`, which holds the `AppBar`, does not run, so the title bar is not "described ... both times"; it is described once. The case where the title bar really is described again the same way is the refresh button: `_reload` calls `setState` in `_ProductListScreenState` (product_list_screen.dart L27), which reruns the whole `build` (L30-69).
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with: "You notice this when you press the refresh button: `_ProductListScreenState`'s `build` runs again and describes the title bar exactly as before, and the title bar stays as it was while the body changes." Add to the claims ledger: "Pressing refresh calls setState in _ProductListScreenState, so its build (including the AppBar) runs again." (source: product_list_screen.dart L27, L30).
